oewn-01756692-v.learner: to make something happen, or make it come to exist.
examples: I know nothing of the effects that such a step might produce
The happiness which this reply produced was such as he had probably never felt before

oewn-02145619-v.learner: to bring something out so that it can be seen.
examples: Mr. Collins readily assented, and a book was produced
Other books were produced, and after some deliberation he chose "Fordyce's Sermons."

oewn-01624592-v.learner: to make or manufacture a thing that people make rather than a natural thing.
examples: The factory produces bicycles and spare parts.
They produce more steel now than they did ten years ago.

oewn-02029396-v.learner: to go or travel somewhere together with someone.
examples: She was to accompany Sir William and his second daughter.
she received an invitation from Mrs. Forster, the wife of the colonel of the regiment, to accompany her to Brighton

oewn-02722040-v.learner: to be there along with an event or a thing.
examples: The talk was accompanied by a slide show.
Heavy rain accompanied the storm.
He accompanied his grandmother through her long illness, sitting with her every day.

oewn-00430033-n.learner: something you do that entertains you and holds your attention.
examples: he acted very wisely in leaving the girls to their own trifling amusements
though this gentleman dislikes the amusement in general, he can have no objection

oewn-07506616-n.learner: the feeling of pleasure you get when something entertains you.
examples: her ignorance and folly had contributed to his amusement
She watched the kitten with quiet amusement.
Dining together every evening was the family's habit.
The hotel is known for good dining.

oewn-05950141-n.learner: anything you hold in your mind as being true.
examples: every day confirms my belief of the inconsistency of all human characters
But do not deceive yourself into a belief that I will ever recede.

oewn-05925333-n.learner: an idea that is not clear or certain but that you trust to some degree.
examples: My belief is that he meant well, though I could not say why.

oewn-01496967-v.learner: to put something in a certain place, whether a real place or not.
examples: Mr. Collins, much offended, laid aside his book
Do you consider the forms of introduction, and the stress that is laid on them, as nonsense?

oewn-02312241-v.learner: to place a duty, a burden, or a punishment on someone.
examples: he scrupled not to lay all the ill consequences of Lydia's flight on her own folly alone

oewn-01547474-v.learner: to set something down so that it lies flat.
examples: She laid the letter flat on the table.
They laid the sick man carefully on the bed.

oewn-07569189-n.learner: a deep sense of what another person is suffering, and sympathy for it.
examples: I cannot consider your situation with much compassion
she did not seem to ask for compassion

oewn-04836781-n.learner: the kind quality of understanding what others suffer and wanting to do something about it.
examples: in a cause of compassion and honour he had been able to get the better of himself
Her compassion led her to work among the poor.

connotation.why: names the trait as a humane one

oewn-07304311-n.learner: a thing that makes people feel surprise and awe.
examples: down they ran into the dining-room which fronted the lane, in quest of this wonder
The old bridge is one of the wonders of the region.

oewn-07525235-n.learner: the feeling that something strange and surprising stirs in you.
examples: The children watched the fireworks in wonder.
She stared at the great hall with wonder.

oewn-05690411-n.learner: the state of wanting to learn more about something.
examples: His wonder about how the machine worked kept him asking questions.

oewn-01793089-v.learner: to make someone feel angry at being wronged.

oewn-05660438-n.learner: the power to choose, to decide, and to mean to do something.
examples: We act by our own will, choosing what we do.

oewn-06556133-n.learner: a legal paper saying what a person wants done with their property after they die.
examples: He left the house to his sister in his will.

oewn-05992539-n.learner: a firm purpose that you hold to.
examples: He had the will to finish the race in spite of the pain.
